video_caption: The video opens with a black screen, then transitions to a white background displaying an oval logo that includes the stylized text "Dr. Zack" above a small circular image with green markings, and "Flat Earth Research" below it; to the right, a cartoon boy in a blue shirt and pants stands with a slight smirk. This is followed by another white screen featuring the prominent, stylized text "STEVE TORRENCE" in green and yellow, with an American flag integrated into the "O" of Torrence, and a yellow-green telescope on a tripod to the right. After a brief black screen, the view changes to a YouTube video player within a web browser, showing a video titled "Flat Earth | Problem Solved (Subtitulado)" (Flat Earth | Problem Solved (Subtitled)). Initially, the video displays a blue background with a wispy white object and the text "...made of five distinct layers!", with the playhead at 0:58 of 8:30. The video then switches to a live-action shot of a man in a dark suit speaking and gesturing with both hands, seated before a laptop with an Apple logo; text overlays identify him as "Sandor Szekely AKA Da Man," which then changes to "Steve Torrence." As the "Steve Torrence" overlay fades, the bottom part of the video player displays new text: "Flat Earth Celestial Clock v3.31 - Tenerife, Spain (Star Trails 360°)."

The video segment opens at 0:02 displaying a Google Chrome web browser window on a desktop, showing a YouTube video with the title "Flat Earth Celestial Clock v3.31 - Tenerife, Spain (Star Trails 360°)" by "Steve Torrance" (66 views, "Suscrito" - Subscribed). The video player shows a simulation of a night sky over a dark, rocky landscape, with numerous concentric blue and white "star trails" circling above, accompanied by a detailed text overlay on the left in light green and white ("Celestial Clock v3.31 (Tenerife, Spain 28.261°, -16.51°)", "Ground location to Sun distance: 8864 miles", "Sun diameter: 36 miles", "Position: 23.435° -90.584°", "In Cancer 0°", "Altitude: 4150 miles", "Moon diameter: 36 miles", "Position: -18.125° 102.441°", "In Capricorn 16°", "Altitude: 4046 miles", "Illumination: 90.96%", "Camera altitude: 1.096 miles, angle 28.5°", "Focal length: 10mm - Sensor size: 36mm", "Sun to Moon distance: 11945 miles", "Sun ahead of Moon angle: 195.60°", "Sun unrefracted elevation angle: 37.214°") and on the right in various colors, showing planetary data ("Tuesday - June 21, 2016 - UTC 18:16", "Mercury: 21.105° -119.637°", "±Altitude: 5267 miles", "Air speed: 109 mph", "In Gemini 13°", etc.). At 0:06, the screen quickly transitions to a different YouTube video, titled "CC V3.31 Do we know the moon is a sphere?" (103 views). This video shows a close-up of a crescent moon against a black background, which then begins to flatten and elongate, appearing to be a disc that becomes progressively thinner and more elliptical, reflecting on a simulated blue water surface as it flattens further. At 0:13, the scene cuts to another flat Earth simulation. This simulation features a low-angle view of dark, textured hills or mountains in the foreground, with a bright, glowing sun-like object moving horizontally above a lighter, flat middle ground (possibly water or ice). The sky is initially dark blue and transitions to a hazy bright blue as the sun moves. Overlaid text on the left updates with new location and celestial data ("Celestial Clock v3.3 (Lake Balaton - Balatonfüred, Hungary)", "Atmospheric refraction: 1.18 @ 10 miles", "Sun diameter: 38 miles", "Position: -3.216° 143.309°", "Libra 7°", "Altitude: 4088 miles", "Air speed: 1652 mph", "Moon diameter: 38 miles", "Position: -1.427° 145.109°", "In Libra 9°", "Altitude: 4166 miles", "Illumination: 2.018%", "Air speed: 1671 mph", "Camera altitude: 0 miles", "Sun to Moon distance: 1043 miles", "Sun ahead of Moon angle: 3.633"), while the right side displays updated planetary information ("Saturday - October 01, 2016 - UTC 23:22", "Mercury: 5.099° 128.885°", "In Virgo 25°", "±Altitude: 5626 miles", "Air speed: 1503 mph", "Venus: -14.744° 108.794°", "In Scorpio 15°", "±Altitude: 18700 miles", "Air speed: 1955 mph", "Mars: -25.827° -83.237°", "In Capricorn 27°", "±Altitude: 11757 miles", "Air speed: 2053 mph"). As the sun moves, the text "Lake Balaton" and "Budapest - Hungary" appears briefly over the central mountains.

The video features a time-lapse simulation from "CELESTIAL CLOCK V3.3 (Lake Balaton - Balatonfüred, Hungary)" displaying a landscape of rolling, ice-capped mountains and water. In the center, white text identifies the location as "Lake Balaton" and "Budapest - Hungary." A bright, spherical sun is initially visible in the sky as the scene begins in daylight. Throughout the segment, the scene rapidly transitions between day and night cycles, with the sun appearing and disappearing below the horizon, causing the landscape to darken and lighten accordingly. Overlaid text provides continuous data: "CELESTIAL CLOCK V3.3 (Lake Balaton - Balatonfüred, Hungary)" and "Atmospheric refraction: 1.18 @ 10 miles" in the top left. The date and time, such as "Sunday - October 02, 2016 - UTC 11:20," update in the top right corner. Two main panels display dynamic information: the left panel (yellow text) shows "Sun diameter: 38 miles," "Position," "Altitude: 4086 miles," "Air speed: 1668 mph," "Moon diameter: 38 miles," "Position," "Illumination: 11.274%," "Air speed: 1676 mph," "Camera altitude: 0 miles," "Sun to Moon distance: 2130 miles," and "Sun ahead of Moon angle: 18.452." The right panel (multi-colored text) shows similar data for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune, including their "Position," "Altitude," and "Air speed." At one point, the screen briefly goes black, displaying the white text "NOT US" before returning to the simulation. The simulation continues to show the sun rising and setting over the landscape, cycling through different times of day across several simulated days, with all numerical data constantly updating.

The video opens with a cartoon landscape featuring a sandy foreground, a road with a church, a green car, a small building, and a city skyline on the horizon. A green tree stands to the left. A man in a dark suit is on the far right, looking at a device in his hands. Above the landscape, a blue sky is depicted with multiple horizontal lines, and the text "Atmosphere or Atmosplane" with a blue curved arrow pointing to the blue sky area. A yellow sun, labeled "Real Sun," appears in the top right, and an orange sun, labeled "Apparent Sun," appears below it and slightly to the left. Yellow arrows illustrate light rays traveling from the "Real Sun" to the "Apparent Sun," then bending downwards towards the man, demonstrating refraction. A black arrow appears next to the "Apparent Sun," indicating it appears lower to the observer. Subsequently, the "Real Sun" moves higher and to the left, and the "Apparent Sun" moves lower and to the right, with the light path bending to show it appearing higher to the man. This entire scenario is then covered by a large red 'X' and a pink bubble containing the word "Wrong," indicating it's an incorrect explanation. The scene resets, and a faint orange sun with a dashed outline appears low on the horizon, then a solid orange sun appears, followed by another to its right with rays. An orange sun (initially labeled "L0," then changing to "LOW") appears low on the horizon to the right, while a yellow sun (labeled "HIGH") appears much higher in the sky. Black arrows show a path from the lower orange sun upwards to the yellow sun and back, and from another low orange sun directly upwards to a yellow sun.

The video segment displays a cartoon-style illustration of a landscape featuring a blue body of water, a city skyline, a church, a green car, and a tree on land. A cartoon man in a dark suit stands on the right, looking at his phone. In the sky, a yellow sun labeled "HIGH" is at the top center, with an arrow pointing down to an orange sun with spikes in the middle of the sky. To the right, another orange sun, labeled "LOW," is positioned closer to the horizon. The text "WHAT MAKES THE SUN GO DOWN A" (WHAT MAKES THE SUN GO DOWN AS IT MOVES AWAY FROM YOU?) is visible at the top, posing a question about the sun's apparent movement.

The video begins with a white screen, featuring a small circular logo in the bottom left corner depicting a stylized figure with a brain. At 00:01, a cartoon-like landscape emerges, showing a road, a body of water, and a light blue sky. On the left side of the road are a small green tree and a church-like building, while on the right, a man in a suit looks at his phone in front of a city skyline. A small yellow, sparkling sun is visible in the top left corner, representing the "real sun." The text "4000 MILES" appears (4000 MILES), indicating a distance. Subsequently, three identical orange, sparkling suns appear sequentially from left to right over the water, lower than the "real sun," illustrating apparent positions. At 00:09, the scene transitions to a scientific diagram of light refraction through a "Rectangular glass slab." A red "Incident ray" enters the glass from "AIR," refracts, and exits as an "Emergent ray," showing "Lateral displacement." Two orange sun-like shapes appear within the glass, seemingly representing the apparent source of light, and the "real sun" remains in the top left. The video then cuts to an underwater view of a swimming pool at 00:14, with lane markers and a red and white floating lane rope. A yellow lightbulb drawing appears above the water, then moves downwards, transforming into a smaller, outlined, then fully yellow and sparkling lightbulb *under* the water, demonstrating the visual effect of refraction on an object's apparent position. At 00:21, a white screen displays the text "IF YOU, GUYS, CAN HELP" (If you guys can help) followed by "DR. ZACK: zikoworld123@gmail.com" (Dr. Zack: zikoworld123@gmail.com), a call for assistance. This is followed at 00:25 by an image of two glasses of water, each with a red straw appearing bent at the water's surface. Above each glass, a small yellow sun appears, and then an orange sun with rays emerges *inside* the water, near the straws, illustrating the apparent position of a light source underwater. Two cartoon people, a man with brown hair and a woman with dark hair, appear below the glasses, looking upwards. The scene transitions to a stylized circular logo animation at 00:32, which gradually reveals "CINEMA 4D" and "ZIK" inside, with the incomplete text "THEOP" (likely part of "THEORY") appearing above it. Finally, at 00:37, a dark screen with white text lists various parameters: "Camera altitude: 0.001 miles", "Camera vertical field of view 97°", "Altitude of sun: 4000 miles", "Elevation angle of real sun: 31.611°", "Ground distance to sun: 6485.6 miles", "Distance to sun: 7619.908 miles", alongside a vertical axis marked with angles from 10° to 90°, and the labels "Without atmosplane (airless)" and "With atmosplane" at the top, implying a comparison of light behavior in different atmospheric conditions.

The video displays two simulated scenarios, each split vertically to compare conditions "Without atmosplane" (or "No atmosplane") on the left and "With atmosplane" (or "Atmosplane") on the right. In the first scenario (0:04-0:16), against a dark background, a "Real Sun" and an "Apparent Sun" are shown as glowing white circles moving along a vertical degree scale (0-90°). Text overlays at the bottom left, which change dynamically, indicate: "camera altitude: 0.001 miles" (camera altitude: 0.001 miles), "camera vertical field of view 97°" (camera vertical field of view 97 degrees), "altitude of sun: 4000 miles" (altitude of sun: 4000 miles), "elevation angle of real sun: 67.278°" (elevation angle of real sun: 67.278 degrees), "real distance to sun: 1661.6 miles" (real distance to sun: 1661.6 miles), and "apparent distance to sun: 4331.386 miles" (apparent distance to sun: 4331.386 miles). The "Apparent Sun" consistently moves at a faster rate and appears higher than the "Real Sun" at corresponding moments, eventually disappearing earlier as a green trapezoidal "ground" becomes visible on the right. The narrator states that the apparent sun appears to move faster and disappears in less than 7,000 miles. The scene transitions (0:16) to a blue sky background, where the "Real Sun" (left) and "Apparent Sun" (right) ascend a vertical degree scale. The "Apparent Sun" starts at 0° while the "Real Sun" is at 35°, and as the "Real Sun" rises at a normal speed, the "Apparent Sun" follows at a higher speed, eventually both reaching approximately 70°. The dynamic text at the bottom left now shows "real distance to sun: 6515.911 miles" (real distance to sun: 6515.911 miles) and "apparent distance to sun: 7845.719 miles" (apparent distance to sun: 7845.719 miles), both values changing as the suns ascend.

The video segment opens with a computer screen displaying an AutoCAD 2016 software interface, showing a technical diagram titled "Sun On The Flat Earth" in English. This diagram illustrates a flat Earth model with an "Earth" point and a "Sun" line above it, marked with hourly points (12PM to 7PM). Various lines represent the "Apparent path of the sun" with angles (e.g., 90.00°, 76.25°, 62.53°, 48.90°, 35.40°, 22.19°) emanating from the "Earth" point to the "Real path of the sun" line, with distances between hourly points (e.g., 951.39, 1080.5, 1370.69, 2079.75, 4072.09) indicated on the horizontal line, increasing with distance from the observer. A brief transition then shows a web browser open to "SunCalc.org", displaying a map centered on Egypt and Sudan with a circular sun path overlay and a red marker. On the left, a sidebar provides "Solar data for the selected location" (English) including "altitude" (90.00°), "azimuth" (41.52°), and coordinates (N 23°26'56.66", E 30°36'37.12") for "21 Jun. 2016 12:00 UTC+2". The video then transitions back to the AutoCAD diagram, zooming in to highlight the increasing distances between hourly points on the "Real path of the sun" (e.g., 951.39 between 12PM and 1PM, and 4072.09 between 5PM and 6PM), emphasizing that the sun travels faster as it moves away from the observer in this flat Earth representation.

The video opens with a first-person perspective shot from a vehicle moving on a multi-lane highway, possibly during a cloudy day, under an elevated concrete overpass. Numerous cars, trucks, RVs, and vans drive on the wet road, moving in both directions, appearing sped up or as a time-lapse, with mountains and hills visible in the background and a large transmission tower to the left. At 00:11, the scene abruptly cuts to a dark, starry sky simulation with a low horizon line. Text overlays appear on both sides of the screen: on the left, white text displays "CELESTIAL CLOCK V3.31 (Tenerife, Spain 28.261° -15.51°)" (Celestial Clock V3.31, indicating the software and simulated location), followed by detailed celestial data for the Sun and Moon (diameter, position, zodiac sign, altitude, illumination, camera details, and distances), with values like "Sun unrefracted elevation angle" (e.g., 25.743°) changing dynamically. On the right, colored text lists various planets (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) with their respective positions and altitudes (e.g., "Mercury: 23.926° 139.7° in Gemini ±Altitude: 6203 miles"), also showing slight changes over time. Throughout this segment, a bright white object (likely the simulated sun or a prominent star) is visible with numerous curving white star trails rotating around it, and the horizon slowly rises from the bottom of the screen.

The video displays a simulated celestial view from Tenerife, Spain, as indicated by the top-left text "Celestial Clock v3.31 (Tenerife, Spain 28.261°, -15.51°)." The scene features a dark, starless sky with a luminous white celestial body (labeled as the Sun, whose distance from the ground location is listed) moving across, leaving a trail of numerous glowing concentric arcs. In the foreground, a barren, grey and brown landscape with a winding path is visible, suggesting a terrestrial or lunar surface. Overlaid text provides extensive astronomical data: on the left, details about the Sun, Moon (diameter, position, altitude, illumination percentage), and camera settings (altitude, angle, focal length, sensor size, distance to Moon, angle ahead of Moon, unrefracted elevation angle) are continuously updated. On the right, the date and time progress from "Tuesday - June 21, 2016 - UTC 9" to "Wednesday - June 22, 2016 - CEST 1" and beyond, while detailed information for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and Uranus (position, altitude, and constellation) is displayed and updated in real-time. The celestial bodies move slowly across the sky, and their associated data changes dynamically throughout the segment.

The video segment displays a computer-generated simulation titled "Celestial Clock v3.31 (Tenerife, Spain 28.261°, -15.51°)" showing a starry sky with long, curved star trails, which appear as white concentric arcs on a dark blue background. In the foreground, a light gray, undulating landscape is visible, resembling a planetary or lunar surface, with a bright, glowing celestial object (possibly the moon or sun) that moves and changes in prominence. Throughout the segment, dynamic textual information is overlaid on the screen; on the left, details like "Ground location to Sun distance: [changing value] miles" (e.g., "9548 miles"), "Moon diameter: 36 miles," "Position: [changing coordinates]," "In Cancer [changing degrees]," "Altitude: [changing value] miles" (e.g., "4150 miles"), "Illumination: [changing percentage]" (e.g., "95.71%"), "Camera altitude: 1.096 miles, angle 28.5°," "Focal Length: 10mm • Sensor size: 36mm," "Sun to Moon distance: [changing value] miles" (e.g., "12066 miles"), "Sun ahead of Moon angle: [changing degrees]" (e.g., "187.723°"), and "Sun unrefracted elevation angle: [changing degrees]" (e.g., "25.163°"). On the right side, the date "Tuesday - June 21, 2016 - CEST [changing time]" and "Wednesday - June 22, 2016 - UTC 23:" are shown, along with a list of planets (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto) and their corresponding changing coordinates and altitudes. From 00:13, a small inset image appears in the bottom right corner, displaying a real-life photograph of circular star trails above what looks like an observatory or building. The simulation's star trails become progressively more defined and numerous, often forming a "tunnel" effect before the sky brightens, eventually closely resembling the concentric patterns seen in the inset photograph, as stated by the narrator who says, "the star trails look exactly like the original picture." The segment concludes with a brief black screen transition, followed by a split-screen view (from 00:30) where the celestial clock simulation is duplicated, showing identical views in both the upper and lower halves, complete with all the text overlays.

The video segment opens with a split-screen display, presenting an identical celestial simulation on both halves, showing a dark sky with numerous concentric white star trails above a subtle, earthy horizon, and a bright white dot representing a celestial body. Overlaid text on the top left indicates "Celestial Clock v3.31 (Tenerife, Spain 28.261°, -15.51°)" (Celestial Clock version 3.31, Tenerife, Spain, latitude 28.261 degrees, longitude -15.51 degrees), along with dynamically updating astronomical data such as "Ground location to Sun distance: 7186 miles," "Moon diameter: 36 miles," and "Camera altitude: 1.096 miles," as well as planetary positions for Mercury and Venus. On the top right, the date and time are displayed, starting with "Tuesday - June 21, 2016 - UTC 0" (Tuesday - June 21, 2016 - Coordinated Universal Time 0), which gradually advances. Throughout the segment, the star trails subtly change their curvature and extent, and the bright celestial body shifts its position, reflecting the continuous progression of the simulated time.

The video segment presents a dynamic simulation of celestial bodies, initially showing white, curved lines against a background that transitions from dark to light blue/gray and back, suggesting changes in sky conditions or time of day. On the left, a detailed text overlay from "CELESTIAL CLOCK V3.31 (Salinas, California 36.688°, -121.652°)" provides real-time astronomical data including the "Ground location to Sun distance," "Sun diameter," "Moon diameter" (later "320 miles (10x actual)"), "Position" coordinates, constellation names (e.g., "In Scorpio 17°"), "Altitude," "Illumination," "Camera altitude," "Focal Length," "Sun to Moon distance," "Moon ahead of Moon angle," and "Unrefracted elevation angle," with values constantly updating. Concurrently, on the right side of the screen, the date and time (e.g., "Saturday - November 12, 2016 - UTC 0:", "Friday - November 11, 2016 - PST 16:") are shown alongside similar data for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune, detailing their positions (e.g., "In Scorpio 18°") and altitudes. A small, circular, bright object appears around 0:10, slowly traversing the screen, labeled by the text "Tracking Moon's position" at the bottom center. Briefly at 0:27, the white curved lines fragment into dark, abstract shapes before resuming their pattern. The scene then abruptly changes to a split screen: an Excel spreadsheet titled "Observacion de Supernova" (Supernova Observation) displaying columns of numerical and textual data on the left, and a 3D wireframe globe on the right, featuring grid lines, named celestial points like "Betelgeuse," "Altair," and "Vega," and numerical labels such as "4000."

The video begins with a 3D animated model of a flat earth, rendered in blue against a black background, rotating to display continents, primarily Europe and parts of Asia and Africa. An open Excel spreadsheet on the left side shows columns of star data, including "Caden," "Equat," and "Type," with a Spanish menu bar and a security warning reading "Advertencia de seguridad Se han deshabilitado las conexiones de datos" (Security warning Data connections have been disabled). White lines extend from the North Pole of the flat earth model, each ending with a small green dot representing a star, some labeled with names like "Polaris," "Vega," "Capella," "Arcturus," "Betelgeuse," "Altair," "Procyon," "Rigel," and "Sirius." Numbers like "4000" indicate star altitudes in miles, and angular measurements (e.g., "93.80°", "84.80°") are marked on a circular grid on the flat earth. The top right corner of the screen briefly displays "AutoCAD 2014." The scene then transitions to a simulated sky view from a ground perspective, labeled "South," with dark mountain silhouettes at the bottom. Numerous white arcs, representing the paths of celestial bodies, traverse the sky, which shifts from light blue to a deeper blue, indicating the passage of time. Overlaying text on both sides of the screen provides data from a "Celestial Clock v3.31 (Rio de Janeiro, RJ)," showing dynamically updating information such as "Ground location to Sun distance," "Sun diameter," "Moon diameter," "Camera altitude," and the positions and altitudes of Mercury, Venus, and Mars. The sun (a bright disc) and the moon (a crescent) are visible, along with numerous star trails, all moving across the simulated sky. The video concludes with a completely dark screen, featuring only the bright sun and crescent moon, with dark, abstract shapes (possibly landmasses or other objects) silhouetted below, illuminated by the sun's glow, suggesting a view from high above.

The video opens with a black screen featuring a subtle, white crescent shape in the center, which gradually brightens and reveals itself to be a detailed crescent moon with visible craters. A small blue icon of a cartoon character, a man in a white lab coat, is positioned in the bottom-left corner throughout this sequence. At 0:14, the perspective abruptly shifts, showing the moon as a flat, disc-like object viewed from its edge, positioned against a blurry, colorful background resembling a distorted Earth. The moon then rotates to reveal its half-illuminated surface, and the camera pulls back to show this moon-disc centered over a dynamic, abstract, and colorful background that warps and shifts, suggesting a flat map or globe with continent-like outlines. This animated background continues to move and change colors around the static, half-illuminated moon-disc until 0:28, when the screen transitions to black, displaying white text that reads "THANKS FOR WATCHING" in the center, with the cartoon icon briefly remaining before fading out.
